idiom_name: Result-typed decisions propagated with ? (Result is #[must_use]); privacy-enforced policy module; tower/axum layer seam
implementation_notes: Rust's contribution is that the failure direction is the path of least resistance: a decision returns `Result<Grant, Deny>` (or `Option<Grant>`), and the standard-library docs state that `Result` is annotated `#[must_use]` precisely because 'it is easy to ignore the return value, thus failing to handle the error', while `?` propagates a denial or a policy error outward so an unhandled decision cannot be read as success. A permissive default has to be written deliberately (`unwrap_or(true)`, `if let Err(_) = check { ... }`, `map_err(|_| Grant::all())`) and is therefore greppable in review. Module privacy keeps the policy the only route in, and the middleware seam (`tower`/axum `layer`, which the axum docs describe as free to return early when 'a request cannot be authorized') applies the decision to every request. What is not provided is the policy data: grants, roles and the decision function are application code, so 'idiomatic' describes the error and default mechanics, not a standard-library authorization system.
pitfalls: A permissive default must be typed out: `unwrap_or(true)`, `is_ok()` used as 'not forbidden', `unwrap_or_default()` on a policy cache whose Default is permissive, and `map_err(|_| Grant::all())` all reopen it - the compiler cannot flag these, so review and lints must.

`#[must_use]` is a warning by default: a crate that denies it (`#![deny(unused_must_use)]`) and clippy's `let_underscore_must_use` are what turn a dropped decision into a build failure, otherwise `let _ = check();` compiles cleanly.

Panics and poisoned locks: a `Mutex` poisoned by a panic returns `Err` from `lock()`, so `unwrap_or_default()` on the whole decision hands back an empty (deny) or a permissive default set depending on the type - treat 'cannot read the policy' as an explicit denial.

Late `?` in a middleware that runs after the handler turns a denial into a 500 and may already have written a response; keep the denying branch in front of the inner service and map errors to a 403/503 response there.

Derived `Default` on grant types: an empty `Vec` is a safe deny, but `Option<Role>` fields combined with `unwrap_or(Role::Admin)` at the call site are a fail-open default in disguise - type the grant as a non-optional value so the deny is expressible only as absence.
